title: The Ramayana of Valmiki
author: valmiki
attributionNote: Traditionally attributed to Valmiki. The poem grew through oral transmission and the surviving recensions differ, so the work is best described as a tradition rather than a single authorial text.
description: The story of Rama, Sita and Ravana in six books: the boyhood and marriage of Rama, his exile, the abduction of Sita, the search through the southern forests, the alliance with the vanaras, and the war at Lanka. Griffith's blank-verse translation follows the Sanskrit cantos closely enough to be quoted by canto. The seventh book is in the companion record 'Ramayana — Uttara Kanda'.
historicalContext: One of the two great Sanskrit epics, composed and transmitted between roughly the fifth and first centuries BCE. Griffith's translation (1870–1874) was the first complete English verse rendering. The Project Gutenberg edition ends with the sixth book, the Yuddha Kanda; the seventh book is held separately in Manmatha Nath Dutt's 1894 prose translation.
availabilityNote: Streamed from Project Gutenberg at read time: the whole plain-text edition is fetched and split at the chapter headings it prints. The 1870 translation by Ralph T. H. Griffith is public domain in the United States. Griffith's edition ends with the sixth book, so the Uttara Kanda is held in the separate record 'Ramayana — Uttara Kanda', in Manmatha Nath Dutt's prose translation.
